title: Air traffic control
eyebrow: Reel 03 · How agents take turns on your Mac
source: claude-control (~/.hammerspoon/bin/claude-control) and the take-control rule in .rules/core_safety.md

beats.say: Several Claude agents share your Mac at once. Air traffic control is the queue that keeps them from typing over each other, or over you.
The rule is simple. Before an agent touches anything you can see or hear, keys, clicks, apps, even the volume, it asks first and waits for a yes.
Asks line up in one queue. Only one agent holds control at a time. The rest wait their turn for up to three minutes, then give up politely.
There are two kinds of ask. Typing or clicking gets the full banner and a soft glow, so hands off. Small changes get a little corner pill you can type through.
You're always in charge. Escape means not now, and the agent waits for your go. Escape twice stops its whole task. Snooze just pushes it back.
Click any banner to jump straight to the thread that's asking. And the urgent flag, which skips the line, is only for stopping a runaway.
Your own automations take a number too, silently. Anything you trigger yourself runs instantly. Only things that run on their own wait in line.
So nothing fights over the keyboard, and you can always see who's flying. That's air traffic control.
